But some of the kids didn’t really want to build the sandcastle, and some of them didn’t have the right tools or enough sand. Also, the grown-ups (the leaders) kept changing the plans and sometimes didn’t give clear instructions. So, when it was time to show their sandcastle to everyone, it wasn’t very strong or finished, and it didn’t look as good as the sandcastles built by other kids who really wanted to do their best.

That’s kind of like why the Italian Army had a hard time in World War II. Some soldiers didn’t feel very excited or prepared, their equipment wasn’t always good, and their leaders sometimes made confusing decisions. So, it was hard for them to do as well as other armies.
